_about: Biblioteca UDC additions to Zotero's schema.json (never edit schema.json). help texts come from zotero.org/support/kb/item_types_and_fields, or are our own where the page has none.

type_help.artwork: A piece of artwork (e.g., an oil painting, photograph, or sculpture). Also use this item type for other types of images or visual items (e.g., scientific figures).
type_help.attachment: A standalone attachment file (e.g., a PDF, JPEG, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, or ODT file). Standalone attachment files have limited functionality in Zotero (e.g., they cannot be properly searched or cited). Always attach files to proper Zotero items.
type_help.audioRecording: Any form of audio recording, including music, spoken word, sound effects, archival recordings, or audio-based scientific figures.
type_help.blogPost: An article or entry posted to a personal blog website. For online articles published as part of a larger online publication (e.g., NYT Blogs), using Magazine Article or Newspaper Article generally yields better results.
type_help.book: A book or similar published item. For government documents, technical reports, manuals, etc., use Report instead. This item type can also be adapted to fit many types of unusual items.
type_help.bookSection: A section of a book. Usually chapters, but also forewords, prefaces, introductions, appendices, afterwords, comments, etc.
type_help.case: A legal case, either published or unpublished.
type_help.computerProgram: A piece of software, an app, or another computer program.
type_help.conferencePaper: A paper presented at a conference and subsequently published in a formal conference proceedings publication (e.g., as a book, report, or issue of a journal). For conference papers that have not been published in a proceedings, use Presentation.
type_help.dictionaryEntry: An entry published as part of a dictionary.
type_help.document: A generic document item. This item type has a poor selection of fields and poor support in citation styles, so it should generally be avoided.
type_help.email: A message sent via email. This type could also be used for other forms of personal communication.
type_help.encyclopediaArticle: An article or chapter published as part of an encyclopedia.
type_help.film: A film or motion picture. Generally, use this type for artistically-oriented films (including fictional, non-fictional, and documentary films). For other types of video items, use Video Recording.
type_help.forumPost: A post on an online discussion forum. Also use this type for items such as Facebook posts or tweets.
type_help.hearing: A formal hearing or meeting report by a legislative body.
type_help.instantMessage: A message sent via an instant message or chat service. This type could also be used for other forms of personal communication.
type_help.interview: An interview with a person, including recordings, transcripts, or other records of the interview.
type_help.journalArticle: An article published in a scholarly journal (either print or online).
type_help.letter: A letter sent between persons or organizations. This type could also be used for other forms of personal communication.
type_help.magazineArticle: An article published in a non-scholarly, popular, or trade magazine (either print or online).
type_help.manuscript: An unpublished manuscript. Use this type for both historical documents and modern unpublished work (e.g., unpublished manuscripts, manuscripts submitted for publication, working papers that are not widely available). Can also be used for other forms of historical or archival documents. This item type can also be adapted to fit many types of unusual items.
type_help.map: A map. Also use this type for geographic models.
type_help.newspaperArticle: An article published in a newspaper (either print or online).
type_help.note: A standalone note. Notes can be used for organizing and annotating in Zotero. If you cite a standalone note, Zotero will use the first 120 characters as the item title (and will treat the note as an author-less and date-less item). Citing notes is not a reliable way to add standalone commentary to a bibliography or reference list.
type_help.patent: A patent awarded for an invention.
type_help.podcast: A podcast (an episode of an audio or video program distributed online, often via subscription).
type_help.preprint: A version of a scholarly or scientific paper that precedes formal peer review and publication in a peer-reviewed scholarly or scientific journal. The preprint may be available, often as a non-typeset version available for free, before or after a paper is published in a journal, through institutional repositories or preprint servers. This item type can also be used for working papers.
type_help.presentation: A presentation made as part of a conference, meeting, symposium, lecture, etc. This item type refers to the presentation itself, not a written version published as part of a conference proceedings (use Conference Paper for such published versions).
type_help.radioBroadcast: An audio broadcast, such as a radio news show, an episode of a radio entertainment series, or similar. Includes broadcasts from online radio stations and audio broadcasts archived online (cf. Podcast).
type_help.report: A report published by an organization, institution, government department, or similar entity. Also used for working papers and preprints distributed through institutional repositories or preprint servers. This item type can also be adapted to fit many types of unusual items.
type_help.standard: A published document describing a standard, or a similar set of industrial or governmental specifications.
type_help.statute: A law or other piece of enacted legislation.
type_help.thesis: A thesis submitted as part of a student applying for a degree (either published or unpublished).
type_help.tvBroadcast: An episode of a television series.
type_help.videoRecording: A video recording. Use this type for general video items that do not fit into one of the more specific video item types (e.g., Film, TV Broadcast), such as YouTube videos or video-based scientific figures.

help.DOI: The Digital Object Identifier of an item. For items other than journal articles, the DOI can be stored in Extra. See Citing Fields from Extra below.
help.ISBN: The International Standard Book Number of a book or other publication.
help.ISSN: The International Standard Serial Number of a periodical or series publication.
help.accessDate: Date an electronic resource was accessed. Typically filled automatically. You can enter "today," "yesterday," and "tomorrow" to quickly enter the corresponding date.
help.applicationNumber: The identification number assigned to a patent application.
help.archive: Mainly for archival resources, the archive where an item was found. Also used for repositories, such as government report databases, institutional repositories, or subject repositories.
help.archiveID: The identifier of the preprint in its repository (e.g. "arXiv:2101.00001").
help.archiveLocation: The location of an item in an archive, such as a box and folder number or other relevant location information from the finding aid. Include the subcollection/call number, box number, and folder number together in this field. For additional tips on citing archival sources in Zotero, see here.
help.artworkMedium: The type of artwork or figure or the medium it was created with (e.g., "Watercolor painting", "Wood sculpture", "X-ray Crystallograph", "Scatterplot").
help.artworkSize: The dimensions of the artwork or figure.
help.assignee: The entity to which a ownership rights for a patent are assigned.
help.audioFileType: The format of an audio or video recording (e.g. "DVD," "CD," "MP3," etc.).
help.audioRecordingFormat: The format of an audio or video recording (e.g. "DVD," "CD," "MP3," etc.).
help.billNumber: The identification number assigned to a proposed piece of legislation.
help.blogTitle: The title of the blog or website containing a post or specific web page.
help.bookTitle: The title of the book, encyclopedia, or dictionary that a chapter, entry, or other book section is published in.
help.callNumber: The call number of an item in a library. For citing archival sources, also include the Call Number in Loc. in Archive (if applicable).
help.caseName: The title of a legal case.
help.citationKey: Citation key of the item (e.g. for BibTeX).
help.code: The name of the code in which a bill or statute is published.
help.codeNumber: The identification number assigned to a piece of legislation in the code in which it is published.
help.codePages: The pages in the code volume containing a bill or statute.
help.codeVolume: The volume number of the code containing a bill or statute.
help.company: The organization publishing a computer program.
help.conferenceName: The name of the conference or meeting where a conference paper or presentation was presented.
help.court: The court where a legal case was argued.
help.date: Date of publication. Use "Accessed" for the date an electronic resource was accessed.
help.dateDecided: The date a legal case was decided.
help.dateEnacted: The date a statute was enacted.
help.dictionaryTitle: The title of the book, encyclopedia, or dictionary that a chapter, entry, or other book section is published in.
help.distributor: The organization distributing a film in a market.
help.docketNumber: The docket number assigned to a to-be-heard legal case.
help.documentNumber: The document identification number assigned to a published transcript or record of a committee hearing.
help.edition: The edition of a work. Where numeric, enter as simple Arabic numeral (i.e., "2" rather than "second").
help.encyclopediaTitle: The title of the book, encyclopedia, or dictionary that a chapter, entry, or other book section is published in.
help.episodeNumber: The episode number of a podcast or TV/radio broadcast.
help.eventPlace: The geographic location of an event.
help.extra: Free field for storing additional information. You can also store additional variables not included in an item’s fields that can be used when making citations and bibliographies . See Citing Fields from Extra below.
help.filingDate: The date on which a patent application was filed.
help.firstPage: The first page of the reporter volume on which a case appears.
help.format: The physical or digital format of the item (e.g. "eBook", "PDF", "CSV").
help.forumTitle: The forum or listserv where a post was made.
help.history: Resources related to the procedural history of a bill or statute.
help.identifier: The identifier of the dataset in its repository.
help.institution: The institution publishing a report or the university granting the degree for a thesis.
help.interviewMedium: For interviews, the format in which an interview was recorded (e.g., "Audio Recording", "Video Recording", "Transcript").
help.issue: The issue number of a periodical. Typically, issues start at 1 at the beginning of each year/volume. If a periodical has only a volume number and no issue number, leave this field blank.
help.issueDate: The date on which a patent is formally issued.
help.issuingAuthority: The authority or office reviewing the application and issuing the patent.
help.journalAbbreviation: The abbreviated title of a journal. When using the Zotero Word or LibreOffice plugins, Zotero can automatically abbreviate titles using the MEDLINE list. Use this field to enter abbreviations using other systems or for generating bibliographies outside of a word processor.
help.label: The recording label distributing an audio recording in a market.
help.language:
The language of publication for an item. We recommend storing these as two letter ISO language codes followed by two letter ISO country codes (e.g., en-US for American English, or de-DE for German).

The Language field is used to determine whether English Title Casing rules should be applied when formatting item titles. If the stored item data is in English (e.g., for translated titles), enter en-US or en-UK, even if the item content is in another language.
help.legalStatus: The legal status of a patent or application.
help.legislativeBody: The legislative body (parliament, senate, etc.) debating a bill, holding a hearing, or passing legislation.
help.letterType: A description of the specific type or purpose of letter (e.g., "Private correspondence).
help.libraryCatalog: The catalog or database an item was imported from. This field is used, for example, in the MLA citation style. Uses of this field are broader than actual library catalogs.
help.manuscriptType: A description of the type or status of the manuscript (e.g., "Unpublished manuscript", "Manuscript submitted for publication", "Working paper").
help.mapType: For maps, a description of the specific type or genre of map.
help.meetingName: The name of the conference or meeting where a conference paper or presentation was presented.
help.nameOfAct: The full title of a statute.
help.network: The network broadcasting a TV or radio show.
help.numPages: The number of pages in a book.
help.number: The number or identifier of the item.
help.numberOfVolumes: The number of volumes in a collective work.
help.organization: The body that publishes the standard (e.g. "ISO", "IEEE").
help.originalDate: The original date an item was published. Enter in ISO format (year-month-day).
help.originalPlace: The geographic location of the publisher of the original version of an item (e.g., the untranslated version).
help.originalPublisher: The publisher of the original version of an item (e.g., the untranslated version).
help.pages: The page range of an item that is part of a larger publication. Also to be used for locators or article numbers in e-journals and ebooks.
help.partNumber: The number of the part (an article published in parts, or a standard divided into parts).
help.patentNumber: The identification number assigned to a patent.
help.place: The place of publication for an item.
help.postType: A description of the specific type of forum post (e.g., "Tweet" or "Facebook comment").
help.presentationType: The type or format of presentation (e.g., "Poster", "Symposium", "Invited address").
help.priorityDate: The priority date of the patent (the date of the first application whose priority it claims).
help.priorityNumbers: The international application number of a patent used for priority rights claims.
help.proceedingsTitle: The title of the conference proceedings where a conference paper was published.
help.programTitle: The title of a radio or TV show of which an episode is part (e.g., "This American Life" or "60 Minutes").
help.programmingLanguage: The programming language a computer program is written in. Note that Computer Program uses the Language field differently than other items.
help.publicLawNumber: The identification number assigned to an enacted piece of legislation. See here for more details.
help.publicationTitle: The title of the periodical (journal, magazine, newspaper, etc.) containing the cited item
help.references: Resources related to the history of a patent.
help.reportNumber: The number of a report. Do not include the words "Number", "No.", "Nº", "№", or similar; these will be added automatically by the citation style.
help.reportType: The type of report (e.g., "Technical report", "CPTO Technical Brief") or thesis (e.g., "Doctoral dissertation", "Ph.D. thesis", "Master thesis"; the word 'thesis' or 'dissertation' should be included where applicable).
help.reporter: The reporter in which a legal case is published.
help.reporterVolume: The volume number of the reporter in which a legal case is published.
help.repository: The repository or server that publishes the item (e.g. "arXiv", "Zenodo").
help.rights: The copyright terms, license, or release status for an item.
help.runningTime: The running time of any type of recording. Enter with the unit (e.g., 120 mins).
help.scale: The scale of a map or model.
help.series: Name of a series that contains multiple publications or presentations (e.g., "Cambridge Studies in Comparative Politics", "Special issue on Advances in Personality Assessment").
help.seriesNumber: The number of an item in a series.
help.seriesText: Additional series text (e.g. "New series"), common in older journals.
help.seriesTitle: Title of a series of articles within one issue of a journal (e.g., a special section or "From the Cover"). "Section Title" would likely be a more appropriate label. See here for an explanation. For citation purposes, this field is currently equivalent to "Series" and is erroneously used instead of series in some item types (e.g., Audio Recording, Map).
help.session: The session of a legislative body in which a bill was introduced, statute was passed, or hearing was held.
help.sessionTitle: The title of the conference session or panel the item was presented in.
help.shortTitle: Short form of the title, often without the subtitle. Used mostly in footnote styles for subsequent citations
help.status: The publication status of an item (e.g., "forthcoming", "in press", "advance online publication").
help.studio: The studio producing a video recording.
help.subject: The title of an email.
help.system: The operating system or platform a computer program is written for.
help.thesisType: The type of report (e.g., "Technical report", "CPTO Technical Brief") or thesis (e.g., "Doctoral dissertation", "Ph.D. thesis", "Master thesis"; the word 'thesis' or 'dissertation' should be included where applicable).
help.title: The principal title of an item. Should be entered in sentence case.
help.type: The type of the item (free text).
help.university: The institution publishing a report or the university granting the degree for a thesis.
help.url: URL (web-address) where the full item was accessed. Do not use this field for links to catalog records (e.g., libraries or Google Books) or abstracts—these should be instead added as links.
help.versionNumber: The version of a computer program.
help.videoRecordingFormat: The format of an audio or video recording (e.g. "DVD," "CD," "MP3," etc.).
help.volume: The volume of a (typically multi-volume) publication an article or chapter is published in. For numeric volumes, enter only a number. If the volume should be cited with a volume title, include the title in this field (e.g,. "2: Organizational Psychology").
help.websiteTitle: The title of the blog or website containing a post or specific web page.
help.websiteType: Rarely used. Describes the genre of a webpage such as "personal blog" or "intranet".

bill.section: The section of a bill or statute being cited.

case.history: Resources related to the procedural history of a legal case.

conferencePaper.place: For Presentations, the place where the meeting was held or the presentation was made. For Conference Papers (published in a conference proceedings), use this field for the place where the proceedings was published. If separate locations are needed for the publication place and the location of the conference, leave this field blank and add Event Place and Publisher Place fields to Extra (see Citing Fields from Extra below).

dataset.type: The type of dataset (e.g. "Survey data", "Genomic sequence").

journalArticle.section: The section of the journal the article appears in.

manuscript.institution: The institution where the manuscript was produced or is held (e.g. for working papers).

preprint.genre: The genre or subtype of the preprint (e.g. "Working paper").

presentation.place: For Presentations, the place where the meeting was held or the presentation was made. For Conference Papers (published in a conference proceedings), use this field for the place where the proceedings was published. If separate locations are needed for the publication place and the location of the conference, leave this field blank and add Event Place and Publisher Place fields to Extra (see Citing Fields from Extra below).

standard.committee: The technical committee that prepared the standard (e.g. "ISO/TC 46").
standard.type: The type of standard (e.g. "International Standard", "Technical Specification").
standard.versionNumber: The version or revision of the standard.

statute.section: The section of a bill or statute being cited.

creator_help.artist: The creator of a piece of artwork or a figure. The author for Artwork items.
creator_help.attorneyAgent: The attorney or agent representing an inventor when filing a patent.
creator_help.author:
The principal author or creator of a work. Enter authors (and other creators) in the order that they should be cited.

Enter names of persons in two-field (Last/Family, First/Given) mode. Enter names of institutions or organizations in one-field mode.
creator_help.bookAuthor: The author of the whole book, when the cited section was written by someone else.
creator_help.cartographer: The principal creator of a map. The author for Map item.
creator_help.castMember: A member of the cast of a broadcast or performance.
creator_help.chair: The chair or moderator of a conference session.
creator_help.commenter: An individual commenting on a blog post.
creator_help.composer: The composer of the music on an audio recording.
creator_help.contributor: Other individuals or entities associated with a work that should not be included in citations (e.g., individuals listed after "with" on a book's cover). Used as the author for Hearing items.
creator_help.cosponsor: Cosponsors or endorsers of a bill or piece of legislation.
creator_help.counsel: The counsel arguing a legal case.
creator_help.creator: The generic creator of a dataset or software.
creator_help.director: The director of a broadcast or recording. The author for Film Recording, Video Recording, Radio Broadcast, and TV Broadcast items.
creator_help.editor: The editor of an item or the broader publication an item is part of (e.g., book, journal). If a distinction is drawn between the textual editor and the managing editor/publishing editor/editorial director (Directeur de la Publication in French), use editor for the textual editor and enter Editorial Director in Extra. See Citing Fields from Extra below.
creator_help.executiveProducer: The executive producer of a series or broadcast.
creator_help.guest: A guest on a podcast, radio broadcast, or TV broadcast.
creator_help.host: The host of a radio or TV program.
creator_help.interviewee: The person being interviewed. The author for Interview items.
creator_help.interviewer: The person asking questions during an interview.
creator_help.inventor: The creator of an invention. The author for Patent items.
creator_help.narrator: The narrator of a recording (e.g. an audiobook).
creator_help.organizer: The organizer of the conference or meeting.
creator_help.originalCreator: A type of Creator. The original creator of a work.
creator_help.performer: The individual performing on an audio recording. The author for Audio Recording items.
creator_help.podcaster: The host of a podcast. The author for Podcast items.
creator_help.presenter: The person giving a presentation. The author for Presentation items.
creator_help.producer: A producer for a film, recording, or broadcast.
creator_help.programmer: The programmer for a computer program. The author for Computer Program items.
creator_help.recipient: The person receiving a letter, email, or message.
creator_help.reviewedAuthor: The name of the author whose work is being reviewed.
creator_help.scriptwriter: The person writing the script for a film or broadcast.
creator_help.seriesCreator: The creator of the TV, radio or podcast series the episode belongs to.
creator_help.seriesEditor: The overseeing editor of a series of items.
creator_help.sponsor: The principal author of a bill or piece of legislation. The author for Bill and Legislation items.
creator_help.translator: The translator of an item. If the same person is both the editor and translator of a work, enter their name as both an Editor and a Translator in separate fields.
creator_help.wordsBy: The individual who wrote the words in an audio recording (e.g., the lyricist or speechwriter).
